RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL  ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Friday, the December 9, 2005/Agrahayana 18, 1927 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Agriculture; Chemicals and Fertilizers; Consumer Affairs, Food
and Public Distribution; Environment and Forests; Food Processing
Industries; Health and Family Welfare; Railways; Steel)
Total number of questions — 20
Revival of Gorakhpur and Sindri
fertilizer units
*241. SHRI RAJEEV SHUKLA: Will
the Minister of CHEMICALS AND
FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are considering the revival of the Gorakhpur
and Sindri units of the Fertilizer
Corporation of India, by setting up gas-
based brownfield fertilizer plants at the
existing sites;
(b) if so, the details of the proposal;
(c) whether it is also a fact that GAIL
has agreed to supply gas to the units by
2010; and
(d) by when the units are scheduled to
be operational?
Complaints against slaughter houses
causing environmental pollution
†*242. DR. CHHATTRAPAL SINGH
LODHA: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) the number of complaints received
by the Central Pollution Control Board and
the State Pollution Control Boards/
Committees during the last three years
regarding environmental pollution caused
by slaughter houses;
(b) the names of complainants and the
details of their complaints alongwith the
names of those against whom each
complaint has been made;
(c) the action taken by the Central
Pollution Control Board and the State
Pollution Control Boards/Committees on
such complaints; and
(d) whether complainants have also
been apprised of the outcome of inquiry?
Antyodaya Anna Yojana in Andhra
Pradesh
*243. SHRI NANDI YELLAIAH: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Society for Elimination
of Rural Poverty has estimated that in
Andhra Pradesh, 23,84,535 families are at
the risk of hunger;
(b) whether at present 12,33,600
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

76
families are covered under the Antyodaya
Anna Yojana scheme in the State;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) the details of the scheme and
guidelines for its implementation;
(e) whether 13,49,990 families are yet
to be covered under this scheme;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) whether Government would take
immediate steps to cover all these families,
including all the left-over families under the
scheme?
CBI raids in hospitals
*244. SHRI DATTA MEGHE: Will the
Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Bureau of
Investigation (CBI) has conducted raids on
certain hospitals in Delhi and other cities;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) the reasons for conducting raids on
these hospitals;
(d) the incriminating documents seized
from these concerned hospitals;
(e) whether any arrests have, so far,
been made;
(f) if so, the details thereof; and
(g) the departmental action so far taken
or proposed to be taken against the
concerned officers of these hospitals?
Linking of Gurgaon/Rewari/Alwar
with Punjab
*245. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have received
any representations to link Gurgaon/
Rewari/Alwar with Punjab by extending/
diverting some of the trains which terminate
at Delhi/New Delhi;
(b) if so, by when; and
(c) if not, the reasons therefor?
Agriculture as knowledge-based
industry
*246. SHRIMATI JAMANA DEVI
BARUPAL:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether agriculture is becoming a
'knowledge-based' industry globally and in
India if remains of subsistance level,
although over 66 per cent of population
depends on agriculture;
(b) if so, whether experts have urged
India to move forward and be globally
relevant like information technology;
(c) whether India is also a major exporter
of several agricultural commodities and has
earned top position in the production of
milk, wheat, fruits and vegetables;
(d) whether Government have
considered setting up more open
universities for agriculture; and
(e) if so, the other steps Government
propose to take in this regard?
M.S. Swaminathan Committee
*247. DR. CHANDAN MITRA: Will
the Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether a Committee headed by the
scientist Prof. M.S. Swaminathan has been
set up to recommend steps to be taken
along the Indian coastline in view of the
Tsunami disaster last year;

77
(b) whether it is proposed to draw a
vulnerability line along the coast and amend
the Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) along
this proposed line;
(c) whether it is proposed that new
construction is to be allowed only beyond
1500 mts. from the coast; and
(d) whether Government have taken
into account its impact on beach tourism
and hotel locations if construction is banned
upto one and a half kms. from the shore?
Increase in prices of pulses
*248. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of AGRICULTURE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is fact that the rates of
pulses are going to be high this year;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether Government have taken any
remedial action to cope up with this
problem?
Polluted lakes in Andhra Pradesh
*249. SHRIMATI VANGA GEETHA:
Will the Minister of ENVIRONMENT
AND FORESTS be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government had surveyed
the polluted lakes in the country during the
last one year especially in Andhra Pradesh;
(b) if so, the details of such surveys
made in each district;
(c) the remedial steps taken and to be
taken by Government in this regard;
(d) whether Government are facing
financial crunch to clean the polluted lakes;
(e) if so, the amount allocated, so far;
and
(f) the amount to be allocated during
the coming year to clear the lakes from
pollution?
Cancer patients in the country
†*250. SHRI LAXMINARAYAN
SHARMA: Will the Minister of
CHEMICALS AND FERTILIZERS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the number
of cancer patients is increasing in the
country;
(b) whether it is also a fact that cancer
medicines are costly and out of reach of
common man; and
(c) the measures Government would
take to provide these medicines to the
common man on reasonable rates?
Use of staple pins in packaging of
edible items
†*251. SHRI VASANT CHAVAN: Will
the Minister of CONSUMER AFFAIRS,
FOOD AND PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION
be pleased to state:
(a) whether the use of staple pins in
packaging of edible items is appropriate;
(b) if not, whether Government are
giving it a serious thought; and
(c) whether Government would bring
an amendment in the law to ban this?
NAFED loans
*252. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI:
SHRI AMAR SINGH:
Will the Minister of AGRICUL TURE
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that NAFED has
disbursed loan of several crores of rupees
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

78
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
to a few firms and if so, the details thereof
including the amount of loans given to each
firm and its grounds;
(b) whether it is also a fact that NAFED
had given bank guarantee or extended loans
to these firms without any collateral,
moveable or immoveable sureties; and
(c) if so, what are the details thereof
and the reasons therefor?
New medicine for malaria
†*253. SHRI BHAGWATI SINGH:
Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government have invented
a new medicine based on plants to prevent
malaria;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) whether Government have
completed the trial process of the said
medicine and by when this medicine would
be available to the common man?
Disease surveillance labs
*254. SHRIMATI N.P. DURGA: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Centres
for Disease Control, United States, will
help India in setting up disease surveillance
labs to track disease out-breaks in the
country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that the
National Drug Authority is also going to be
set up to regulate standards for the
manufacture, supply, pricing, licensing and
use of medicines in India;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) what are the other agreements that
India agreed to enter with CUS, United
States, during his recent visit to that
country?
Institute for checking quality of wheat
and rice
†*255. SHRI RAM JETHMALANI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of CONSUMER
AFFAIRS, FOOD AND PUBLIC
DISTRIBUTION be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that an Institute
has been entrusted with the responsibility
of testing the quality of wheat and rice lying
in the stores of Food Corporation of India;
(b) if so, the name of the institute and
the reasons for its selection; and
(c) the amount fixed for the institute for
carrying on the responsibility and whether
the above institute has been selected from
a panel of institutes?
Shareholding pattern of VSP
*256. SHRI S.M. LALJAN BASHA:
Will the Minister of STEEL be pleased to
state:
(a) the shareholding of Government in
Visakhapatnam Steel Plant;
(b) the other investments or stakes in
Visakhapatnam Steel Plant by Government;
(c) whether there is any proposal to
transfer the stake of the Central
Government to the State Government; and
(d) the details of present value of the
Visakhapatnam Steel Plant?

Procurement of materials by South
East Central Railway
†*257. SHRIMATI KAMLA
MANHAR: Will the Minister of
RAILWAYS be pleased to state:
(a) whether the zonal headquarters of
South-East Central Railway located at
Bilaspur has been fully empowered to
procure various materials to be used in the
said zone;
(b) if not, the reasons therefor and by
when such powers will be delegated;
(c) whether any preference will be given
to the State industries in the procurement
of various materials to be used in this zone,
and initiative will be taken by the Railways
for setting up the industries producing such
materials in case such industries are not in
existence at present; and
(d) whether this zone has approached
the Government of Chhattisgarh in this
regard, if so, when and the details thereof?
PM's Task Force on drug prices
*258. DR. KARAN SINGH:
DR. T. SUBBARAMI
REDDY:
Will the Minister of CHEMICALS
AND FERTILIZERS be pleased to state:
(a) whether PM's Task Force on making
the medicines affordable has asked
Government to cut by half the 16 per cent
excise duty levied on retail price of
medicines;
(b) whether the excise duty is currently
levied at 60 per cent of retail price;
(c) whether the final report submitted
by the Task Force also states that ceiling
prices should be fixed for 314 essential
ingredients taken from a list of 354 prepared
by the Health Ministry; and
(d) whether drugs with 70 per cent
market share would be de-branded?
Rural healthcare and education
*259. SHRI  S. ANBALAGAN: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have made any
initiatives for improvement in rural
healthcare and education in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
achievements made thereon;
(c) whether it is a fact that the country
is still lagging behind countries like China
in development of rural healthcare and
education; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and the
concrete steps proposed to be initiated
thereon by Government?
Iron ore produced in India
†*260. SHRIMATI SUSHMA
SWARAJ: Will the Minister of  STEEL be
pleased to state:
(a) the quantum of total deposits of 'iron
ore' available in India;
(b) whether 'iron ore' is exported from
India;
(c) if so, the quantum of 'iron ore'
exported duirng the last three years;
(d) if this pace of export continues, after
how many years 'iron ore' will be exhausted;
(e) whether any conrern has been
expressed by some on this export; and
(f) whether Government propose to
restrict this export?
